title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as sufficient grounds for an armed stop. A license plate camera flagged a stolen Camaro, and that flag set in motion a response that ended with two 19-year-olds handcuffed at gunpoint beside a car that turned out not to be the stolen one. The failure sits at the handoff between the system's output and the human decision to escalate, where a database hit was allowed to stand in for confirmation that the car in front of them was the car in the alert.

The gap was visible in the reporting itself. Deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car they were watching, so instead of resolving the mismatch they called backup. A single confirmed plate read before weapons were drawn would have caught the error, and so would a rule that an unreadable plate stops the escalation rather than adding to it. The system did what it was built to do, which was flag a plate, and the stop proceeded on a visual resemblance that was never checked against the thing the system had actually flagged.

What is not established is whether any procedure was broken. The sheriff's office said supervisors will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed, and that review has not produced a finding. The account of the stop comes from the two men, the plan to hire an attorney is a stated intention rather than a filed claim, and the complaint process they were given information about is a process, not an outcome.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies stopped two 19-year-olds, Anthony and Julian, after mistaking Anthony's Camaro for a stolen car. Deputies drew guns, handcuffed them, and at least five patrol cars and a helicopter were involved. The sheriff's office said license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a matching car, but deputies and the helicopter could not read its plates, so they called backup. After the men were handcuffed, deputies realized it was the wrong car.

Julian said a deputy pushed him down and he had cuts and scrapes. Anthony's mother, Leslie, said she plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. The sheriff's office said supervisors, including the district captain and lieutenants and sergeants, will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
